title: Huawei Open-Sources OpenPangu-2.0-Flash
hook: Huawei open-sourced OpenPangu 2.0's Flash tier — a 92B-parameter, 6B-active MoE model with 512K context, weights, inference code, and training ops all released — with a 505B flagship still to come.
key_points: OpenPangu-2.0-Flash: 92B total parameters, 6B active (mixture-of-experts), 512K-token context window.
Released openly: model weights, inference code, and training operations — not just weights.
A larger flagship, OpenPangu-2.0-Pro (505B total, 18B active), was announced as coming later in July.
Huawei says more open-source components will follow later in the year.
content_html: Huawei added another entry to the wave of large open-weight releases from Chinese labs, open-sourcing the Flash tier of its OpenPangu 2.0 model family.
extra_html:
What shipped

OpenPangu-2.0-Flash is a mixture-of-experts model with 92B total parameters and 6B active per token, plus a 512K-token context window — and Huawei released the weights, inference code, and training operations, not just a checkpoint. A larger flagship, OpenPangu-2.0-Pro (505B total, 18B active), is coming later in July, with more open-source components promised through the rest of the year.

Why it matters

Large, long-context MoE models with full training-op releases — not just inference-ready weights — lower the barrier for others to reproduce or build on the recipe, not merely run the model. It's part of a broader pattern this year of major labs, especially Chinese labs, treating open-weight releases as a competitive front rather than an afterthought.
